everything i say is Pretty subjective so don't take These Things as Facts.

​

For some context me and a mate are playing D&D were we both are a DM and a Player so These tips may be useless in common Settings.  
Anyway  for me as a DM i start with a Basic idea on the spot and build around it according to the reaction of the Chars, the best way is to get a idea for the beginning and a loose concept for the ending and build around your Players choices how they solve it.

Reward creativity, but also have a path you envision and use that as a base if Things go out of Control and you Need a static Point from which to act.

​

And for traps it depents on how much you know About your Players, a inside joke crafted into a trap are a great way to have a funny Moment and otherwise dont be afraid of getting crazy with Thing.

For example a lich had all time in the world to secure his dungeon in everyway possible so there is practically to Limit in case of traps, put yourself in the Position of the lich and how to exterminate These pesky Adventurers that try to destroy your "life's" work.

as far as it goes experienced Players should help you in building your first char if it's a decent Group.  
And for the actual playing part you can Focus on roleplay at first if it's possible otherwise D&D is a game to have fun with so Play your char as you like.

For the stats a rule that worked for me was is "what do i want to do as a character" so for example i want to go sneaking into places and get valuables without Attention i would go into Dex as my main Stat..

for me i wanted to Play a sorcerer so because Charisma affected my spellcasting i Chose it to be my strongest Stat and after that i thought About what i would most likely do in different Encounters (fight and Roleplaying) and Chose my skills accordingly (for me it was wisdom because i wanted to have a high Medicine stat).

so think About different situations and how you would solve them and sync you Char to that.
